To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human monoclonal antibody 1-3A, which is specific to the S2 region of the SARS coronavirus spike protein, is able to neutralize a broad range of SARS viruses, including those with mutations in the receptor binding domain.
we have generated neutralizing human monoclonal antibody against highly conserved domains of the SARS spike protein.
human monoclonal antibody against highly conserved HR1 and 2 domains of the SARS spike protein are more broadly neutralizing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of neutralizing human monoclonal antibody (HmAb) epitopes on the spike (S) protein of Severe Acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-Co-V).
developing a panel of broadly neutralizing human monoclonal antibody (HmAb) therapeutics and subunit vaccines against SARS-CoV and other enveloped viruses.
the identification and development of neutralizing human monoclonal anti-SARS-CoV antibodies for the prevention and treatment of the SARS disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human monoclonal antibody (HmAb) 4A8, produced from a convalescent SARS patient, is a highly neutralizing and broadly reactive HmAb.
human monoclonal antibody against the conserved regions of SARS-CoVs are more broadly neutralizing than the human monoclonal against S1 domain of SARS-CoVS.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S2-specific HmAbs are more broadly neutralizing.
the S2 domain is a good target for vaccine development.

the S2-specific HmAbs have a higher neutralizing breadth, which is likely due to their binding to the HR1 and HR 2 domains of the S protein, which are highly conserved among different SARS-CoV isolates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S2 domain, in particular the HR2 region, contains epitopes that are highly conserved among different SARS-CoV strains and that these epitopes can be targeted by neutralizing antibodies.
HmAbs that target highly conserved regions of SARS-CoVs, such as the HR1 and HR1 domains of the S protein, are more broadly neutralizing.
antibodies that bind to the SARS spike protein at the conserved regions of S2 are more broadly neutralizing.
